title: Sex, lies and (alleged) Chinese spies: the Nvidia CEO’s affair
description:
The Venn diagram of technology, geopolitics and national security = the Nvidia scandal.

Something we didn’t have on our bingo cards for 2026: The boss of the AI firm Nvidia is being investigated by his own company after being caught having an affair with a woman alleged to be a Chinese spy.

Jensen Huang’s admitted the affair with Alice Huang (no relation) and China’s denied that she’s a spy. Jensen Huang’s friend, the US President Donald Trump, has backed him. So, where does this leave one of the most powerful men in the world? And what does this all mean for US national security? We break it all down with Shawn Yuan from the BBC’s Global China Unit.

Instagram: @bbcwhatintheworld Email: whatintheworld@bbc.co.uk WhatsApp: +44 330 12 33 22 6 Presenter: Hannah Gelbart Producer: Emilia Jansson and Mollie Perella Editor: Verity Wilde
summaryZh: 本集 BBC 節目《What in the World》探討 Nvidia 執行長黃仁勳與 MegaSpeed 執行董事 Alice Huang 的婚外情醜聞，以及美方疑慮其涉嫌為中國間諜對美國國家安全的影響。美國情報機構正在調查 Alice Huang 是否利用此關係將遭禁運的高階 AI 晶片走私至中國。儘管 Nvidia 表示未洩漏任何機密，中國外交部亦否認指控，且美國總統川普公開挺黃仁勳，但消息仍導致 Nvidia 股價下跌 4% 的市值，顯示出美中科技競爭中複雜的人性與地緣政治威脅。
summaryEn: This episode of BBC's What in the World examines the scandal surrounding Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's admitted affair with Alice Huang, managing director of MegaSpeed, who is alleged by US intelligence to be a Chinese spy. The podcast explores allegations that she used the relationship to access restricted AI chips, posing national security risks to the US. While Nvidia stated no company secrets were compromised, China denied the spy claims, and US President Donald Trump backed Jensen Huang, the news still caused Nvidia's stock to tumble by 4%, illustrating how human relationships intersect with geopolitical tech rivalries.
